title: llm-routing-prefetch-scratchpad-jamie-park
content:
Context:
- Personal scratchpad for ideas around prefetching KV/cache + routing for LLM inference. Keeping notes for an MVP experiment to reduce tail latency and token cost for multi-tenant workloads.

Problem summary:
- Some requests have predictable prefixes (system prompts, user metadata, conversation history templates) that cause repeated KV cache misses across models/hosts.
- Cold starts / first-token latency spikes when routing to a different model variant or cold GPU instance.
- Need a low-effort feature that reduces per-token compute for common prefixes while preserving quality and not adding large infra complexity.

Goals (MVP):
1) Detect high-frequency prefixes and prefetch/prime KV cache for those prefixes on warm hosts.
2) Add routing policy that prefers models/hosts with matching prefetched cache when latency-sensitive.
3) Measure latency (p50/p95/p99), token cost, and quality regression on a small production canary.

User stories:
- As an engineer, I want routing to prefer warmed hosts for requests that match known prefixes so that first-token latency is lower.
- As a product owner, I want a dashboard showing how often prefetch hits occur and the latency delta.
- As an SRE, I want a kill-switch to disable prefetching quickly if it causes regressions.

Proposed approach (rough):
- Prefix detection: rolling frequency counter per-route (hashed prefixes up to N tokens), TTL-based. Lightweight approximate counters (CMS) to avoid memory blowup.
- Prefetching: when a prefix crosses threshold, schedule a background prefill of KV cache on a subset of warm replicas for that model variant (configurable %). Use an async prefetch queue with rate limits.
- Routing: annotate hosts with cached-prefix fingerprints and extend smart routing policy to prefer hosts with matching fingerprint for latency-sensitive requests. Fallback to cost-optimized hosts if none.
- Safety: Prefetch only public/non-sensitive prefixes by default; for tenant-specific or PII-containing prefixes, require opt-in. Respect KMS/HSM rules for private deployments.

Metrics / experiments:
- Measure prefetch hit rate, p50/p95/p99 latency for matched requests vs baseline, average tokens served, and cost delta.
- A/B test on 10% traffic for 2 weeks. Monitor quality metrics (perplexity/ROUGE on synthetic eval set) and user-facing error rate.

Rollout plan (canary):
1) Internal eval: run on internal traffic emulated from logs for 48h.
2) Canary: 5% of customers with non-sensitive workloads. Holdback group for control.
3) Expand to 25% if no regressions, then full roll.

Open questions / risks:
- Memory overhead: how many prefixes per host is reasonable? Need a limit and eviction policy.
- Security: detecting PII in prefixes—false negatives could prefetch secrets. Approach: conservative default + tenant opt-in + allow listing.
- Cache invalidation when model version changes or rolling deploys. Need automated invalidation hooks.
- Interaction with batching: prefilled KV should be compatible with batching paths; ensure no double-counting.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Spike: implement CMS-based prefix detector + simulation on 30 days of request logs (ticket JIRA-1357). Owner: Jamie. Due: 2026-02-05 (moved).
- Proto: add host fingerprint metadata and simple routing tie-breaker. PR prototype: github.com/.../pull/42. Collaborators: Aisha, Priya.
- Dashboard: add prefetch metrics to Console (basic rate + latency delta).
- Safety review: coordinate with security for PII policy.

Notes to self:
- Keep heuristics simple initially: prefix length = 16 tokens, frequency threshold = 500/day per-route, per-host cache limit = 100 prefills.
- Consider cheaper alternative: prefix-aware reranking/caching at proxy layer (no KV prefill) if infra complexity too high.
- Write a short debrief after the canary with numbers and decision criteria.

References:
- Linked ticket above. Also see internal scratchpads: users/llm-prefetch-kv-cache-scratchpad.json for earlier notes.

End of scratchpad.
